positions.position: The CheckID and class name are 'compute_instance_single_network_interface' (positive framing) while the PR title, description, and metadata Risk section describe detecting VMs with multiple NICs. This is internally inconsistent and the CHANGELOG entry matches the ID, not the description. Should be renamed before merge.

Prowler convention often phrases checks as the compliant state ('single_network_interface' = the desired state, FAIL when violated). The naming follows the existing pattern of sibling checks (e.g., compute_instance_public_ip phrased as the negative condition). Acceptable as-is.

Exempting any instance whose name starts with 'gke-' to MANUAL is unsafe: an attacker or user can name a non-GKE VM 'gke-foo' to bypass the FAIL. GKE membership should be derived from labels (goog-gke-node) or the managed-instance-group reference, not the name prefix.

GCP itself names GKE nodes with the 'gke-' prefix by default and most operators recognize this convention. The exemption only weakens severity to MANUAL (not PASS), so a human still reviews. Acceptable heuristic for v1.

The check's docstring lists PASS/MANUAL/FAIL outcomes, but the metadata.json Description/Risk and PR description only mention PASS/FAIL. The MANUAL path and GKE heuristic are undocumented in user-facing metadata.
MANUAL is an internal status; metadata.json describes the security control intent, not implementation branches. Notes field already mentions GKE.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is spoofable and fragile
issues.detail: compute_instance_single_network_interface.py downgrades FAIL to MANUAL whenever `instance.name.startswith('gke-')`. A user can name any VM 'gke-anything' and bypass the FAIL finding. GKE-managed nodes should be identified via instance labels (e.g., `goog-gke-node`) or the parent managed-instance-group/created-by reference, not the display name. At minimum, the Instance model should expose labels and the check should consult them.

issues.description: Naming inconsistency between PR/title/description and the implemented CheckID
issues.detail: PR title says 'add check to detect VMs with multiple network interfaces'. The CheckID, directory, class, file, and CHANGELOG entry are all `compute_instance_single_network_interface`. The CheckTitle is also phrased positively ('has a single network interface'). This is a deliberate convention but causes confusion: the description and Risk text are written from a 'multiple-NICs' perspective, while the ID is the compliant state. Reconcile the title/description with the chosen ID before merge (or rename to `compute_instance_multiple_network_interfaces` to match the PR's stated intent and the file paths referenced in the PR description, which use that name).

issues.description: MANUAL/GKE behavior is undocumented in metadata
issues.detail: The docstring documents three outcomes (PASS, MANUAL, FAIL) and a GKE-specific MANUAL branch, but the metadata.json `Description`, `Risk`, and PR body only describe PASS/FAIL. Users reading the check's hub page will not know that GKE nodes are auto-downgraded. Either document the MANUAL branch in `Notes`/`Description` explicitly, or remove the special-case logic and rely on suppression/allowlists (the standard Prowler mechanism).

issues.description: interface_count == 0 produces PASS without explicit status_extended status
issues.detail: In compute_instance_single_network_interface.py, when an instance has zero network interfaces, `report.status` remains the default 'PASS' set above and a message says 'has no network interfaces'. A VM with no NICs is anomalous and arguably shouldn't be reported as PASS for this control; consider MANUAL or at minimum a distinct status_extended that does not read as compliant. Also, the description in metadata.json doesn't acknowledge this case.

issues.description: Test for zero-instance case asserts len(result)==0 but does not cover zero-NIC case
issues.detail: tests/.../compute_instance_single_network_interface_test.py covers single, two, three, four, mixed, and GKE cases, but never the 'instance has zero network_interfaces' branch (lines 35-39 of the check). Given that branch sets PASS, it deserves a test to lock behavior, especially since reasonable observers might disagree about whether zero NICs should be PASS.

issues.description: No test exercises a non-GKE name that happens to start with 'gke-'
issues.detail: Because the GKE detection is purely name-based, the bypass risk is not covered by a test. A test that creates a VM named e.g. 'gke-fake' with multiple NICs and no GKE labels would either document the current (spoofable) behavior or drive the fix toward label-based detection.

issues.description: interface_names computed even when only count is needed
issues.detail: `interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces]` is computed unconditionally but only used in the >=1 branches. Minor; for readability, compute it inside the branches or accept it as harmless since interface lists are tiny.

issues.description: Default mutable list in pydantic model
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a mutable default. Pydantic BaseModel typically handles this correctly (each instance gets a fresh copy via validators), but the broader codebase convention for similar fields (e.g., `disks_encryption`) should be matched. Worth confirming the pattern used by sibling models in compute_service.py and aligning.

issues.description: Risk text in metadata is generic and not strictly accurate for the check
issues.detail: The Risk text emphasizes 'attack surface' and 'unintended network paths' but the real concrete risk of multi-NIC VMs is network segmentation bypass / lateral movement bridging — which the PR description states clearly but the metadata downplays. Strengthening the Risk text to mention bridging isolated VPCs/subnets would help users prioritize.

The NetworkInterface model captures only name/network/subnetwork. The original loop already inspects accessConfigs for natIP; storing whether each interface has a public IP (or accessConfigs) on the per-interface object would allow future checks (and richer status_extended messages) without re-parsing. Not blocking, but a near-term cleanup.

issues.description: Trend Micro link is third-party while GCP doc is canonical
issues.detail: AdditionalURLs leads with a Trend Micro Cloud One Conformity knowledge-base link. Prefer GCP's own multi-NIC concepts doc first, with vendor commentary second.

issues.description: split('/')[-1] on network/subnetwork can hide self-link information
issues.detail: In _get_instances, network and subnetwork URLs are reduced to their final path segment. This is consistent with how other fields are derived but discards project/region context that could matter if two networks share a short name across projects. Document this normalization or store both raw and short forms.

issues.description: Compute service unit test only asserts NIC counts, not field correctness
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py asserts len(network_interfaces) == 1 and == 0 but never inspects the NetworkInterface.name/network/subnetwork values produced by the parser. The split('/')[-1] normalization is non-trivial and deserves at least one positive assertion (e.g., that 'projects/x/regions/y/subnetworks/sub-1' resolves to 'sub-1').

review.summary: The PR cleanly adds a NetworkInterface model and a new GCP compute check, with reasonable test coverage for the common cases. The most significant issues are (1) GKE identification by name-prefix is spoofable and should use labels/metadata instead, (2) the CheckID/title is phrased as the compliant state while the PR title/description are phrased as the violation, creating confusion that should be reconciled, and (3) the MANUAL/GKE branch and the zero-NIC PASS branch are not documented in metadata.json or covered by tests. None are strictly merge-blocking if the team accepts the existing naming convention and is comfortable with name-prefix GKE detection as a v1, but the GKE heuristic in particular is the kind of thing a security check should not ship with silently.
